title: eforecast node, GPU and storage health

list.name: gpu
list.label: GPU (physical UUID)
list.description: Cards are chosen by physical UUID. An ordinal names a different card on every node, and the allocator refuses one outright.

description: A16-06. Node, GPU and storage health for the lab. GPU series are keyed by physical UUID because that is the only device identity this system accepts.

panels.title: Workspace free
panels.description: A ratio, not a byte count: the lab workspace and a second workstation's are different sizes, so a fixed threshold would be wrong on one of them. Alerts under 10%. Blank means the filesystem could not be stated, which usually means it is not mounted.

panels.title: Workspace free bytes
panels.description: The trend is what tells you whether 15% free is recovering or on its way to zero.

panels.title: GPU utilisation
panels.description: Whole-card utilisation. With time-slicing this is the card's total, not any one Pod's share -- see the note at the bottom.

panels.title: Worker Jobs not finished
panels.description: Bounded by the executor at 32. Blank means the cluster API could not be reached, in which case running Jobs are unaffected but none can be launched or observed.

panels.title: Longest pending Pod
panels.description: A pending Pod holds nothing and has started nothing, so it is safe -- but it is not progressing. The executor's status says whether it is the node, the image or a volume.

panels.title: Source availability
panels.description: 0 means we could not read that source; its panels are then blank, not zero. A source this installation does not use (a broker, a cluster) is left out.

panels.title: What these GPU numbers can and cannot tell you

options.content:
**Per-card, not per-Pod.** DCGM reports what a physical card is doing. With whole-card allocation -- which is what the worker pilot does -- one card maps to one attempt, so these graphs are that attempt's.

**Under time-slicing or MPS they would not be.** Several Pods share one card, DCGM still reports one set of numbers for it, and the driver does not attribute utilisation per process in a way that can be split honestly. If GPU sharing is ever enabled (A16-07), these panels remain the card's totals and must be read that way. Inventing a per-Pod utilisation from them would be a fabrication, so none is shown.

**Memory is the exception**: per-process GPU memory is attributable, and the worker's own observer records it for the attempt that holds the card.
